text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Statistical corrections like that on the 1996 budget deficit have happened before, Statistics Finland says; estimate errors are caused by incomplete preliminary information.
- Finnish wholesaler and retailer Kesko has made another appeal to the European Court of Justice, saying the European Commission decided to unravel Kesko's merger with retailer Tuko too hastily. @
- Irish farm ministry proposes bone meal contaminated by mad cow disease be transported to and destroyed in Finland. Finnish authorities have not made any decision yet.
- Some police tasks may be dropped due to lack of resources and changed crimes, Interior Minister Jan-Erik Enestam says.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Finnish power group IVO is worth 15-20 billion markka, a British analyst estimates; this might bring problems to any merger plans betweens oil group Neste and IVO because Neste would not be ready to pay more than 13 billion markka. @

- Unnamed specialist says Amer's decision to redeem K-shares was not based on economic reasons and so may encounter legal difficulties; also says lifting the conversion rate from 1:1.2 to 1:1.5 may be questionable.
- Tax on alcohol will be cut in phases, budget director Erkki Virtanen at Social and Health Ministry says.
- Shops will need soon more employees, but not all workers laid off during the recession will get their jobs back, says Heikki Ropponen, director at the retail employers federation. @
AAMULEHTI
- State-owned Postipankki bank's destiny should also be considered in restructuring of state financing institutions, cooperation with a foreign partner is an option, bank's CEO Eino Keinanen says.
- State has become a popular guarantee-provider for loans to first-time home buyers.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Bicycle manufacturer Tunturi Oy is a strong brand and would be interesting to invest in, says Salvatore Grimaldi, CEO of Swedish bicycle manufacturer Monark Stiga. @
DEMARI
- Budget cuts proposed by finance ministry are hard to comprehend, says Jouni Backman, second minister of interior ministry.
- Value-added tax hike on public transport is unacceptable, transport ministry says.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Nokia is expected to make a profit of H2 3.12 billion before tax and minorities, analysts polled by Swedish news agency Direkt say.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
